title: GM 2.7L turbo (L3B, L2R): ticking from the cam carrier, misfire, worn exhaust roller follower
summary: GM bulletin 25-NA-037: a tap or tick from the exhaust side of the cam carrier, sometimes with P0300-P0304 or P050D, from needle-bearing axle pin wear in an exhaust roller follower. Pull the cam carrier, check every exhaust rocker for roller play, and replace the whole set if one is bad.

steps.text: Use a stethoscope to see if the tick is on the exhaust side of the cam carrier. If it is, a worn exhaust roller follower is the suspect and the cam carrier has to come off.
Remove the cam carrier, then the exhaust rockers and exhaust hydraulic lash adjusters.
Hold each exhaust rocker body and try to push the roller up and down. Noticeable play in the bearing means it's worn. If unsure, compare with a known-good intake rocker.
It's unusual for more than one to fail, but if any exhaust rocker is bad, replace the whole set. Note which position failed.
Look for loose roller bearings in the head and remove them; each follower has 10. If any turn up in the oil pan, use GM bulletin 22-NA-074 to check for internal engine damage.
Check the exhaust cam lobe under the failed rocker against its neighbors. Scoring or premature wear means replace the camshaft.
Reinstall the cam carrier per service information.

body: The bulletin's model/year table doesn't extract cleanly; the ranges here follow its brand-and-model order (Colorado and Canyon from 2023, Silverado and Sierra 1500 from 2019, CT4 from 2020). Confirm the engine RPO against page 1 of the bulletin.

sources.title: Service Bulletin 25-NA-037: Diagnostic Tip on Abnormal Engine Ticking or Tapping Noise from Cam Carrier Area And Possible Misfire or Rough Run - DTC P0300 and/or P050D
